case_name: R.M. Yellatti v Assistant Executive Engineer
respondent:
Assistant Executive Engineer
Supreme Court of India

7 November 2005
Appeal (civil) 5124 of 2004
The Judgment was delivered by : S. H. Kapadia, J.
1.  The appellant questions the correctness of the judgment of the High Court of judicature at Karnataka at Bangalore whereby the High Court, in Appeal, allowed the writ petition filed by the Assistant Executive Engineer (SD-I), Athani and set aside the order of the Labour Court dated 27.10.1999 directing reinstatement with 50% back wages from the date of the award till the date of reinstatement.

facts: Appellant was appointed as a daily waged earner by the Assistant Executive Engineer on 26.11.1988.
He worked up to 20.6.1994, on which day his services were terminated.

He claimed that he had continuously worked for more than 240 days immediately prior to 20.6.1994 (date of termination) and that his services were wrongly terminated without complying with the provisions of section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
The industrial dispute was referred by the State Government to the labour court vide reference under section 10(I)(c) of the 1947 Act.
issues: Whether the management was justified in removing the claimant from service w.e.f. 20.6.1994?
To what reliefs the claimant was entitled for?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that he had continuously worked for more than 240 days immediately prior to 20.6.1994 (date of termination) and that his services were wrongly terminated without complying with the provisions of section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
He contended that the management suppressed the Nominal Muster Rolls (NMRs) which indicated that he had worked for the entire period between 22.11.1988 to 20.6.1994.
respondent_arguments: The management resisted the reference by filing its counter statement, contending that the appellant was not a worker in terms of section 2(s) of the 1947 Act and consequently, he was not entitled to claim benefit of section 25-F of the said Act.
It was submitted that the 'Irrigation department' was not an 'industry' under the 1947 Act.
court_reasoning: The labour court found on facts and on the basis of evidence led before it that the appellant had worked with SD-1 at Athani continuously for more than 240 days prior to 20.6.1994 (date of termination);
It was observed that the management had suppressed material evidence from the Court.
holding: The labour court directed the management to reinstate the appellant into service as a daily wager with 50% back wages from the date of the award till the date of reinstatement.
The division bench quashed the award passed by the labour court in favour of the appellant and set aside the order of the learned Single Judge.
